items.lease_says: Assignment and subletting need Owner's consent and Owner has a recapture right and a 50 percent profit share, but Tenant may transfer without consent to affiliates, subsidiaries and successors, and may rescind its request to defeat a recapture.
items.proposed_response: Apply a net worth test to all consent-free affiliate and subsidiary transfers (not only successors), delete Tenant's right to rescind after Owner elects recapture, confirm the 50 percent share of transfer profit without the sale-of-business carve-out, and correct the paragraph lettering and cross-references in Article 52.

quotes.text: Tenant may, without Owner’s consent and on not less than ten (10) days prior written notice to Owner

an entity which shall be an “affiliate”, “subsidiary” or “successor” (each as hereinafter defined) of Tenant and the provisions of Paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of this Article shall be inapplicable to such transaction

items.standard: Tenant may not assign the lease or sublet any part of the premises without Landlord's prior written consent. Before consenting, Landlord may take back (recapture) the space. If Tenant sublets or assigns for more than it pays, Landlord receives at least half of the profit.
items.why: The consent-free affiliate and subsidiary transfer carries no net worth test (only successors must meet one), Tenant can withdraw its request to defeat recapture, and the 50 percent share excludes consideration paid for the business in a sale of Tenant's business. Paragraph lettering in Article 52 is inconsistent (two "(a)" paragraphs; cross-references to (f), (h) and (j) do not match), which should be fixed.

positions.response: Limit use to general, executive and administrative offices; list any other use the tenant needs as a specific, approved exception.
positions.standard: The premises are used only for general, executive and administrative offices, with no change of use without Landlord's consent.

positions.departs_if: Tenant may make non-structural alterations without consent above a low threshold, or Landlord's consent cannot be withheld except for structural or building-system work.
positions.response: Require consent for all non-decorative alterations; if a consent-free category is kept, cap it at a small cost per project and exclude anything touching building systems or structure.
positions.standard: Tenant needs Landlord's prior consent for all alterations except purely decorative work (painting, carpeting), uses contractors Landlord approves, and pays Landlord's reasonable review costs.

positions.departs_if: Tenant has no removal obligation, or removal applies only to items Landlord designates at the time of consent and Landlord failed to designate them.
positions.response: Require removal of specialty alterations at Tenant's cost, whether or not Landlord designated them at the time of consent.
positions.standard: At the end of the term Tenant removes its specialty alterations (for example vaults, raised floors, internal staircases, supplemental HVAC) and repairs the damage at its cost.

positions.departs_if: Increases are capped (a fixed percentage per year on all or controllable expenses), the base year is grossed up in Tenant's favor without the same for comparison years, or Tenant pays no operating expense escalation.
positions.response: Remove the cap, or limit it to controllable expenses at no less than 5 percent per year on a cumulative basis.
positions.standard: Tenant pays its proportionate share of increases in operating expenses over a base year, with no cap on controllable expenses.

positions.departs_if: Tenant pays no tax escalation, or the base tax year is reset or reduced in a way that shifts tax increases to Landlord.
positions.response: Keep Tenant's proportionate share of tax increases over the base tax year, without reductions for later abatements that benefit only Landlord.
positions.standard: Tenant pays its proportionate share of increases in real estate taxes over a base tax year.

positions.departs_if: There is no security deposit, the deposit reduces regardless of Tenant's payment history, or Landlord's right to draw is limited beyond a default after notice.
positions.response: Require the letter of credit, and make each reduction conditional on no default having occurred.
positions.standard: Tenant posts cash or an unconditional letter of credit, Landlord may draw on it after a default, and any reduction (burn-down) applies only if Tenant has never been in default.

positions.departs_if: Liability limits are below 5 million dollars, Landlord is not an additional insured, or the waiver of subrogation runs only in Tenant's favor.
positions.response: Raise the liability limits, add Landlord and its managing agent as additional insureds, and make the waiver of subrogation mutual.
positions.standard: Tenant carries commercial general liability insurance of at least 5 million dollars per occurrence (primary plus umbrella), names Landlord and its managing agent as additional insureds, and both parties waive subrogation.

positions.departs_if: Landlord gives a broad indemnity (for example for any act in the building), or Tenant's indemnity is limited to its gross negligence.
positions.response: Keep Tenant's indemnity for its use of the premises and limit any Landlord indemnity to Landlord's negligence or willful misconduct.
positions.standard: Tenant indemnifies Landlord for claims arising from Tenant's use of the premises and its people. Landlord's indemnity, if any, covers only its negligence or willful misconduct.

positions.departs_if: Landlord's liability reaches its other assets, or Landlord is exposed to consequential damages.
positions.response: Limit recovery to Landlord's interest in the building and exclude consequential damages.
positions.standard: Landlord's liability is limited to its interest in the building, and Landlord is never liable for consequential damages.

positions.departs_if: Monetary cure periods are longer than 10 days after notice, Landlord must send more than one notice, or non-monetary cure periods are longer than 30 days without a diligence condition.
positions.response: Return the cure periods to 5 to 10 days for rent and 30 days for other defaults, with one notice.
positions.standard: Tenant has about 5 to 10 days after notice to cure a failure to pay rent, and 30 days after notice to cure other defaults, extended only while Tenant diligently pursues a cure.

positions.departs_if: Tenant may terminate if restoration takes less than 12 months, or rent abates beyond the unusable space.
positions.response: Extend Tenant's termination trigger to at least 12 months and tie rent abatement to the unusable part of the premises.
positions.standard: Landlord restores the building and premises after a casualty. Tenant may terminate only if restoration is not finished within a long outside period (12 months or more), and rent abates only for the unusable space.

positions.departs_if: Holdover rent is below 150 percent, or Tenant is never liable for consequential damages from holding over.
positions.response: Raise holdover rent to at least 150 percent, rising after 30 to 60 days, and keep Tenant liable for damages after notice and a short grace period.
positions.standard: If Tenant stays after the term ends, it pays at least 150 percent of the last rent, rising over time, and is liable for Landlord's damages if it stays past a short grace period after notice.

positions.departs_if: The lease gives Tenant a renewal, expansion, right of first offer or refusal, or termination right, or sets renewal rent below fair market value.
positions.response: Confirm each option is approved; price renewals at fair market rent, make options personal to the original tenant, and void them during a default.
positions.standard: Tenant has no renewal, expansion, first-offer or early termination rights unless Landlord approves them, and any renewal is at fair market rent.

positions.departs_if: Another state's law governs, or there is no mutual jury waiver.
positions.response: Choose New York law and add a mutual waiver of trial by jury.
positions.standard: New York law governs, and both parties waive a jury trial.
